headline: Typhoon Dujuan makes landfall near Tokyo with 180 km/h gusts and torrential rain, while a 10-state US flood corridor continues to escalate and Kīlauea opens new eruptive fissures in Hawaii.
overview: Typhoon Dujuan, Japan's 25th typhoon of the year, is striking eastern Honshu on September 21–22 with violent winds and extreme rainfall, threatening the Tokyo metro area with flooding and landslides. Across the United States, the Midwest–Ohio Valley mega-flood corridor is intensifying with fresh rainfall-driven flash flood emergencies spreading across southeastern Ohio and central West Virginia, while the Mississippi and Illinois river systems face new moderate-to-major crests through late September. Separately, Kīlauea volcano on Hawaiʻi opened new eruptive fissures last week that remain active, and Anak Krakatau in Indonesia produced a dramatic ash column nearly 10 miles high.

events.title: Typhoon Dujuan Strikes Eastern Japan — Tokyo Region Under Flood and Landslide Warnings
events.summary: Typhoon Dujuan, carrying sustained winds and gusts approaching 180 km/h (112 mph), made landfall along Japan's eastern Pacific coastline on September 21–22, directly threatening the Tokyo metropolitan area and the Izu Islands. Weather data shows Tokyo recording 171.8 mm of precipitation alongside the storm, consistent with a major typhoon passage, and the Japan Meteorological Agency has issued flood and landslide warnings across the Kanto region. Mass evacuation advisories were issued and the Tokyo Game Show was shut down a day early as authorities urged residents to shelter in place.

events.title: Midwest–Ohio Valley Mega-Flood Intensifies — Fresh Rainfall Drives New Flash Flood Emergencies in Ohio and West Virginia
events.location: Southeastern Ohio, Central West Virginia, and Indiana, USA
events.summary: Active overnight and morning thunderstorms on September 21 have triggered a new wave of flash flood warnings across southeastern Ohio counties — including Athens, Gallia, Meigs, Vinton, Washington, Morgan, Perry, and Muskingum — and across at least seven counties in central and northwestern West Virginia including Kanawha, Roane, Calhoun, and Wirt. NWS Charleston issued a broad Flash Flood Watch covering portions of both states through midday, with numerous roads closed and streams continuing to rise from excess runoff. Indiana rivers including the Wabash (approaching a record flood stage near Bluffton) and the Saint Marys River (at moderate flood stage through September 26) remain significantly elevated, reflecting the sustained severity of this multi-state corridor.

events.title: Mississippi and Illinois River Systems Escalate — Major Flooding Forecast on Wapsipinicon, Rock, and Iowa Rivers Through Late September
events.summary: The broader Midwest river flood corridor has escalated further on September 21, with the Wapsipinicon River near DeWitt now forecast to reach major flood stage through September 27, and the Rock River at Moline forecast for moderate flooding beginning Monday evening through September 25. The Iowa River is under new flood warnings at multiple gauges in Louisa, Johnson, and Washington counties, with the English River at Kalona in major flood as of September 20. Mississippi River flood warnings have been extended through September 27–28 across stretches from Missouri to Illinois, with additional flood watches pushed out to September 25–26 for downstream gauges at Burlington and Gladstone, representing a downstream progression and intensity increase from prior reports.

events.title: New Mexico and Southwest Flash Flood Threat Expands — Monsoon Surge to Bring Multi-Day Flooding Risk Through September 26
events.location: New Mexico and Far West Texas, USA
events.summary: NWS Albuquerque has issued a Flash Flood Watch covering a large portion of central and northern New Mexico — including the Albuquerque metro area, Sangre de Cristo Mountains, Jemez Mountains, and the Rio Grande Valley — valid from Tuesday through Wednesday evening, September 23. NWS El Paso extended a companion Flood Watch over south-central New Mexico and Far West Texas including Las Cruces and El Paso, active through September 23. AccuWeather forecasts a surge of tropical moisture from Mexico pushing northward from September 22–26, increasing the risk of repeated flash flooding — a significant threat given that three people were already killed by flash flooding in the region on September 16.

events.title: Anak Krakatau Blasts Ash Nearly 10 Miles High — Indonesia's Sunda Strait Volcano Surges in Intensity
events.summary: Anak Krakatau has produced an exceptionally large ash eruption, sending a column nearly 10 miles (approximately 16 km) into the atmosphere — a dramatic escalation beyond the eruptive activity that prompted the search for missing journalists earlier this week. The eruption was captured in satellite imagery and reported by ScienceDaily, with the volcano ejecting both ash and volcanic gases visible from orbit. Indonesia's volcanic monitoring authorities have maintained elevated alert levels for the Sunda Strait volcano, which sits between the islands of Java and Sumatra.

events.title: Kīlauea Erupts New Fissures in Halemaʻumaʻu Crater — Lava Flows from Multiple New Vents
events.summary: Kīlauea volcano opened new eruptive fissures on the northwest wall of Halemaʻumaʻu crater on the nights of September 14–15, 2026, separate from the established vent complex at the summit. USGS Hawaiian Volcano Observatory monitoring overflights confirmed a shiny grey lava flow erupted between September 14–16 from several new vents, with updated reference maps issued on September 16. The eruption remains confined to the summit caldera within Hawaiʻi Volcanoes National Park and does not currently threaten populated areas, but represents a new phase of activity at Kīlauea.

events.title: M6.5 Earthquake Strikes Fox Islands, Aleutian Islands — Tsunami Alert Issued and Cleared
events.location: 169 km W of Nikolski, Aleutian Islands, Alaska, USA
events.summary: A magnitude 6.5 earthquake struck the Fox Islands segment of Alaska's Aleutian chain at 14:19 UTC on September 17, at a depth of 98 km, approximately 169 km west of the remote village of Nikolski (population 18). USGS initially flagged a tsunami alert for the event, though the final USGS alert level was rated green, indicating no significant threat materialized; 8 felt reports were filed. The earthquake occurred in one of the world's most seismically active subduction zones and is the largest seismic event recorded globally in the past seven days.
